nm_ruidoso_area.blurb: The Ruidoso area is made up of many smaller crags and boulder spots within about an hour of the mountain town of Ruidoso, roughly two hours east of Socorro and an hour northeast of Alamogordo. The cooler mountain air gives relief when nearby desert crags run hot. Bouldering accounts for over half the climbs, with sport and trad making up most of the rest and a few top-rope lines. Boulder problems run mostly V0 to V3, while the roped routes center on 5.10 with plenty of 5.8 and 5.9 and a few harder. Monjeau Peak holds the most climbs, and its rock is granite, with summer the best time there. Moon Mountain Meadows, Capitan Gap and Alto Lake Boulders follow.

ny_catskills_ice.blurb: Catskills climbing in New York is mostly ice, spread across Kaaterskill Clove, Stony Clove, Platte Clove and Deep Notch, with a smaller number of mixed lines and a couple of boulders. Ice grades run from WI2 to WI6 and cluster at WI3 and WI4, while the mixed climbs range from M4 up to M9. Platte Clove holds the most climbs, followed by Stony Clove and Kaaterskill Clove. Stony Clove is split into East and West sides and is described as the most popular ice area in the Catskills.

ut_big_bend_bouldering_area.blurb: Big Bend is a boulder cluster in Grand County near Moab, along River Road off Highway 128. The rock is Wingate sandstone, which is porous and weak when wet. Approaches are very short, landings are good, and most problems are not too highball. Grades are described as conservative, with many V0s and V1s feeling hard. Problems run from V0 to V11, with most between V1 and V7. October through March is the best season, though bouldering is possible year-round; summers are very hot, and the area is often sunny and crisp in the cooler months. Flat Top Boulder holds the most climbs, followed by The Black Box, Block Top Boulder and Chaos Boulder.

ut_lower_buckhorn.blurb: Lower Buckhorn is the down-canyon half of Buckhorn Wash in the northern San Rafael Swell of south-central Utah. The wash is a deep, long sandstone canyon, and its climbing mostly follows crack systems, with sport routes starting to appear on faces that have enough features. Trad dominates here, mostly 5.9 to 5.11 with some easier and harder lines, alongside a little sport, some bouldering and a few aid lines. Pine Canyon holds the most climbs, followed by Dylan Wall, Vertical Smile Wall and Private Pizza Wall.
